topicTitle: NEB Class 11 Physics — Refraction Through Prisms — 2024
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Derive the relation δ = i + e − A for refraction through a prism.
questions.solution:
At the first face the ray deviates by (i − r₁); at the second by (e − r₂). Total deviation δ = (i − r₁) + (e − r₂) = (i + e) − (r₁ + r₂).

From the quadrilateral geometry inside the prism, r₁ + r₂ = A (the prism angle). Hence **δ = i + e − A**.
questions.knowledgeNote: At minimum deviation the ray passes symmetrically: i = e and r₁ = r₂ = A/2.

questions.question: Derive the expression for the refractive index of a prism in terms of the angle of minimum deviation.
questions.solution:
At minimum deviation δm: i = e and r₁ = r₂ = r = A/2.

Snell at the first face: n = sin i / sin r. From δm = 2i − A → i = (A + δm)/2.

Therefore **n = sin((A + δm)/2) / sin(A/2)** — the prism formula, used in spectrometers to measure n.
questions.knowledgeNote: This is the standard spectrometer experiment: measure A and δm, compute n — know it as a procedure, not just algebra.

questions.question: A prism of angle 60° has refractive index 1.5. Calculate its angle of minimum deviation.
questions.knowledgeNote: δm rises with both A and n — flint glass deviates more than crown for the same prism angle.

questions.question: Draw the i–δ curve for a prism and explain why there is only one angle of minimum deviation.
questions.solution:
δ falls steeply as i grows, bottoms out at δm, then rises slowly — a U-shaped curve.

There is a single minimum because δ(i) is symmetric about the symmetric-ray path (i = e); moving i either way from that point increases δ — the curve's unique turning point.
questions.knowledgeNote: Near δm the deviation barely changes with i — that stationary reading is why spectrometers lock onto it easily.

questions.question: Show that for a small-angled prism, the deviation is δ = (n − 1)A.
questions.solution:
For small A at near-normal incidence, Snell's law linearises: i ≈ nr₁ and e ≈ nr₂.

δ = (i − r₁) + (e − r₂) = (n − 1)(r₁ + r₂) = **(n − 1)A**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Thin-prism δ is independent of i — every ray through it deviates by the same fixed amount.

questions.question: What is angle of minimum deviation? Write two factors affecting it.
questions.solution:
**Minimum deviation δm** is the smallest angle by which a prism can turn a ray, reached when the ray passes symmetrically.

It increases with (1) the **prism angle A** and (2) the **refractive index** of the material (and falls for longer wavelengths — red deviates least).
questions.knowledgeNote: δm increasing toward violet is exactly what spreads white light into a spectrum.
